nodes.title: The four LIVE pilot scripts read field by field (Learning; one fresh Opus reader per script, same question list as the staged pass): 782 spoken fields read, 79 faulted (10.1%), 7 untrue, 48 giveaways, 0 wrong keys in about 123 cards. Per script: c4-ch05-t01 26 of 178, c5-ch02-t01 23 of 204, c5-ch02-t02 18 of 205, c6-ch06-t01 12 of 195. Worst: all 12 yes/no cards in c4 are keyed 'No', so a child who always says 'nahi' passes every misconception probe. Untrue examples: a rule that the bottom number equals the line's gaps (false on a 0 to 2 line); 'adding every side always works' (false for curves); 'no piece gets a fraction name' over a board showing 1/2. These scripts were in production (releases 16 to 21) and had been through four judged director runs.

Four judged director runs (17 to 20), each with four Opus judges reading 16 lessons, did not find what one field-level read of the same four scripts found: 79 faulted fields, 7 untrue sentences, and a lesson whose yes/no keys are all 'No'. A director run judges the conversation (does she listen, does the screen match her words, is the answer graded right) on the paths a simulated child happens to walk; it does not judge whether each authored sentence is true, simpler, or gives a later answer away, and a rule-based child never exploits an all-'No' key. The scale gate therefore needs both: a script that has passed a full independent read, and a director run on it.

Approval lane, rounds 2, 2b and 3 (generated by main, judged by Studio with two Opus judges under rubric v2, a second judge only after a first pass). Round 2: 26 topics, 22 candidates ($0.043); 6 stored, 4 refused by checks before a judge, 12 by judges. Round 2b (three instrument topics, $0.004): 0 of 3 stored (unit faults in the spec). Round 3: 19 topics, 18 candidates ($0.029); 2 stored, 6 refused by checks (4 geometry-term or mixed-script strings, 2 values off their ticks), 10 by judges (6 wrong fact or missed mix-up, 2 register, 1 engine layout, 1 angle engine limit). Lane total $0.175 of the $0.25 cap; 13 of the 34 scripted topics have an approved game. About 92k tokens per judge run.

The generated-game lane stops running in rounds after round 3, at 13 approved topics. The yield fell from 6 of 22 to 2 of 18 and the remaining refusals are 'misses the mix-up' and engine limits, which a prompt cannot fix and which cannot be checked without an executable mal-rule (Studio's predicate agreed with judges on 6 of 25). Seven topics are on the no-game list with what an engine would need. From here a topic gets a game one at a time: when an engine gains the capability it needs, or when Games builds a family mode with a playable mal-rule, each judged by two judges. A lesson with no approved game stays on the board. Reverse if: Games' modes also fail two judges at this rate over three modes; then games are not the route to showing a mix-up and the board and the teacher carry it.
